TC/RC, Treatment charges and refining charges, is the cost of converting copper concentrate into refined copper, paid by copper mines to smelters, which is an indicator reflecting the supply/demand of copper concentrate market. Chinese copper smelters and overseas copper mines negotiate on term TC/RC every year. In China, the majority of copper concentrate is imported on term basis, and the minority is on spot basis. The profit of copper smelters is highly related to the level of TC/RC. The sales revenue of core business of copper smelting enterprises (monitored by CNIA) in China increased by 18.67% YoY to 482.6 bln yuan in Jan.-Nov. 2012, while the pre-tax profit decreased 6.1 bln yuan YoY. 2 www.antaike.com

#### **Copper Market Commentary** 

###### **Copper price rebounds, but lack of continuous support** 

Copper price fluctuates in the high level in Jan 2013, but has no unilateral up trend under the combined effects of good news from the macro and worries about market consumption. 

LME copper price rebounded in the end of 2012, and went back to USD8,000/t on the first trading day of 2013. After that, copper price fluctuated in the range of USD7,950/t and 8,200/t. Copper price rose by 3% on the last trading day of Jan. 2013 compared to the last trading day of Dec.2012. 

The average prices of LME cash month copper and 3 month copper were USD8,049/t and USD 8,082/t, up by 1.09% and 1.18% MoM or 0.07% and 0.30% YoY, separately. 

SHFE copper price continued to follow the trend of LME and began to rise after the New Year’s Festival. SHFE copper price rose by 2.9% at the last trading day of Jan. 2013 compared to the last trading day of Dec.2012. 

The average prices of SHFE cash month copper and 3 month copper were 58,009yuan/t and 58,279yuan/t, up by 1.54% and 1.68% MoM, but down by0.64% and up by 0.44% YoY, separately. Domestic consumption was weak on copper spot market and was basically at a discount, resulting in a certain constraint on copper future prices. The monthly average price of Antaike’s spot copper quotes was 57,785 yuan/t in Jan. 2013, up by 1.4% MoM. 

From a technical point of view, each index, like moving average, chart and etc., shows upturn trends, but lack of continuous rebounding power. On the whole, copper price still has no continuous rebounding power but the macro gives support for copper price. It is estimated that the monthly average price of SHFE 3 month copper will fluctuate in the range of 59,000 yuan/t and 59,500 yuan/t and LME and LME 3 month copper will fluctuate between USD8,200/t and USD8,250/t 

Chinese economic data continues to be good, forming a support for copper price. The preliminary HSBC PMI, a gauge of nationwide manufacturing activity, is adjusted to 52.3 in January, 0.4 percentage points higher than preliminary figure 51.9. A reading above 50 indicates expansion from the previous month, while a reading below 50 indicates contraction. The index has now been in expansionary territory for three straight months, signaling growth for China's manufacturing sector. The preliminary January figure, a 24-month high, adds to recent signs of a rebound in the world's second-largest economy and could help boost market confidence in China's outlook for this year. 

On the whole, we have not seen an overall improving signs in nonferrous metals industry and it still needs time to have effects on the real economy for Chinese pro-growth policies.

###### **Chinese refined copper production maintains its high level** 

According to data released by China Nonferrou

s Metals Industry Association, domestic refined copper output reached 560kt in Dec 2012, up by 10.2% MoM and 23.7% YoY. During Jan to Dec 2012, refined copper output amounted 5.82Mt, up by 12.1% YoY. Data released by the NBS showed that refined copper output was 580kt in Dec 2012, with y-o-y rise of 22.4%; refined copper output amounted to 6.06Mt during Jan to Dec 2012, up by 10.8% YoY. Besides, according to Antaike’s statistics, copper cathode output of domestic 12 enterprises reached 416.7kt in Dec 2012, up by 8.05% MoM and their combined ouput amounted to 4.23Mt in the whole year 2012, up by 9.37% YoY. Among them, copper cathode output of JCC, TLYS, Jinchuang Group and Yunnan Copper accounted for 28.12%, 21.41%, 14.58% and 8.79%, respectively. 

Above data from three organizations showed that domestic refined copper output appeared a great rise in Dec and in 2012. On one hand, adequate raw material easily available ensured the mass production of refined copper; on the other hand, some smelters may increase production to achieve annual target at the end of 2012. 

Antaike estimates that refined copper output won’t create another new high in January 2013, but still at a high level. 



###### **Chinese refined copper imports still at a rational level, but net import down** 

According to data released by China’s Customs, china imported 239kt refined copper in Dec. 2012, down by 4.7% MoM and 41.3% YoY. Imported refined copper amounted to 3.40Mt in 2012, up by 20.0% YoY. The month on month decline of Chinese imported refined copper was mainly caused by worries

about the uncertainties about trade future. But the imported data is within the expectation. It is estimated that Chinese imported refined copper will decline in 2013 with domestic economy picking up, relative easing monetary policies and decreasing demand for financing copper. As for January imported data, refined copper imports will has a year on year decline under the situation of weak real consumption and lower demand for stockpiling before the Spring Festival Holidays. 

China exported 25kt refined copper in Dec 2012, with a month on month rise of 21.5% and year on year rise of 7693.9%. Chinese exported refined copper amounted to 274kt in 2012, up by 75.3% YoY. Chinese exported refined copper was still rising at a high level. The reasons for the changes are as follows: firstly, policy adjustment for processing trade with imported materials has gradually showed a certain effects; secondly, LME copper price is higher than domestic; finally, domestic refined copper is still in surplus supply. It is estimated that refined copper exports will be still at a high level in January 2013, as a result net refined copper import won’t be high. Net import of Chinese refined copper was 213kt in Dec 2012, down by 47.5% YoY. 

Data from China’s Customs still showed that Chinese imported copper scraps were 443kt in Dec 2012, down by 5.7% MoM and 0.8% YoY.

Copper scraps imports amounted to 4.86Mt, up by 3.7% YoY. Chinese imported copper scraps had a certain increase in the next half of 2012, but which couldn’t change the supply shortage situation. Currently, import enthusiasm for copper scraps is not high due to downstream weak consumption. China imported 935kt copper concentrates, up by 66% YoY and 13% MoM. The great rise of Chinese imported copper concentrates was mainly stimulated by high spot TC/RC in the third quarter of 2012, at about US$80. Domestic copper scrap supply was tight and domestic smelting and refining capacity was expanding. ###### **Copper consumption** As the Report went to be published, the output of main copper end-using products has not been released by the NBS. The data we obtained (including autos, air conditioner, transformer, telecommunication cable and power cable) showed that the output of most copper end-using products had month on month rise, except for telecommunication cable. Output of air conditioner and power cable in Dec 2012 increased by 25% and 19% YoY, showing improving signs of domestic consumption. It is estimated that power industry will still be the main driving force for Chinese refined copper consumption in 2013, with higher growth rate than 2012. The end of home appliance promotion policies in Chinese rural areas in Jan. 31 2013 may make some restrictions on refined copper consumption. Investment in power generation decreases, but investment in power grid is flat. According to data from China Electricity Council, in 2012, the completed power investment was 746.6 billion yuan, down by 1.9% y-o-y. Among them, investment in power generation and grid was 377.2 billion yuan and 369.3 billion www.antaike.com 7 Copper Monthly No. 194 yuan, down by 3.9% or up 0.2% compared with 2011, respectively. Of power generation investment, investment in hydropower was 127.7 billion yuan, up 31.5% y-o-y; investment in thermal power was 101.4 billion yuan, down 10.5% y-o-y. Investment in wind power was 61.5 billion yuan, down by 31.8% y-o-y, ending the rapid growth trend since “the 11th Five Year” period. Investment in Chinese property industry was 7.1804 trillion yuan, nominal up by 16.2% y-o-y, 0.5 percentage points lower than that in Jan to Nov and 11.9 percentage points lower than that in 2011. Among them, investment in residential houses was 4.9374 trillion yuan, up by 11.4% y-o-y, 0.5 percentage points lower than that in Jan

to Nov, accounting for 68.8% of the total investment in real estate. In 2012, floor space under construction was 5734.18 mln sq.m, up by 10.6% y-o-y. Starting floor space of houses was 1773.34 mln sq.m, down by 7.3% y-o-y, 0.1percentage points higher than the decline rate in Jan to Nov, of which starting floor space of residential houses was 1306.95 mln sq.m, down by 11.2% y-o-y. Completion floor space of houses was 994.25 mln sq.m, up by 7.3% y-o-y, 6.8 percentage points lower than that in Jan to Nov, of which completion floor space of residential houses was 790.43 mln sq.m, up by 6.4% y-o-y. On the whole, the contribution to the overall refined copper consumption of Chinese property industry was limited because china housing controls will remain tight. 

###### **Copper market outlook** 

The global economy is improving, especially Chinese economy data is getting better, which forms a great support for copper price. Antaike estimates that the monthly average price of SHFE 3 month copper will move in the range of 59,000 yuan/t and 59,500 yuan/t and LME and LME 3 month copper will fluctuate between USD 8,200/t and USD 8,250/t 

Due to adequate raw material supply and expanded refining capacity, domestic refined copper output will maintain its high level, at 520kt in Jan 2013. Refined copper consumption will be slightly influenced in Jan 2013 because some refined copper consumers were in half shutdown near the Spring Festival Holidays, but with year on year growth slight up. Net import will maintained at a rational level. On the whole, domestic supply will still be in a small surplus, at 60kt in Jan 2013.
